chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Is-haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The first of what the believer is bestowed with is that forgiveness is granted for the one who followed his coffin.
ai.seo_question: What is the first reward bestowed upon a believer who is followed by others at their funeral?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing the funeral procession (*janazah*) as a primary occasion for communal intercession and spiritual merit. The phrase 'first to be honored' (*awwal ma yutahafu bihi*) underscores the immediacy of this reward, linking the social act of following the deceased directly to the divine forgiveness of the followers' sins, thereby reinforcing the Shia emphasis on communal solidarity (*ta'awun*) in rites of passage.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The first of what the Believer is Bestowed with is the Forgiveness for the one who followed his coffin’.
en.sarwar: 3. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
the first gift for a deceased believing person is forgiveness for those who escort him to his grave.”
